 :JUDGMENT:

This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.4,09,013.90/ for the damages caused to the Maruthi Suzuki Swift Car bearing Reg.No.KA51 SCCH 15 3 MVC No.1082/2023 MJ7383 in the Road Traffic accident.
2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
The Petitioner is the RC owner of the Maruthi Suzuki Swift Car bearing Reg.No.KA 51MJ7383.

That on 09.01.2022 at about 7.30 p.m., when Petitioner's son along with his friends, was driving the Maruthi Suzuki Swift Car bearing Reg.No.KA 51 MJ7383 on Bengaluru - Kanakapura main road, Lakshmipura Grama and when they reached Navagraha village, at that time, one Innova Car bearing Reg.No.KA01 AE0728 driven by its driver came in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life and without giving any signal hit the front portion of the Petitioner's Car bearing Reg.No.KA51MJ 7383 and caused the accident.

Due to the impact,
Petitioner's Maruthi Suzuki Swift car was completely damaged and not in a condition to drive on the road.
The accident had occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car.

SCCH 15 4 MVC No.1082/2023 For repairing the said vehicle, the Petitioner had spent a sum of Rs.4,09,013.90/.
The said accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending Innova Car bearing Reg.No.KA01AE0728 by its driver and the Respondent No.1 being the policy holder, the Respondent No.2 being the owner and the Respondent No.3 being the insurer of the car are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.

sentences.text: In pursuance of service of Notice to the Respondents, the Respondent No.1 and 2 remained absent and they were placed exparte.
The Respondent No.3 had appeared before the Court through its Counsel and filed its Objection statement to the main Petition.

The Respondent No.3 in its Objection Statement denied the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car and damage caused to the Swift Car and expenses incurred for the repair of the said car.
Further it SCCH 15 5 MVC No.1082/2023 contended that the alleged car had not all involved in the alleged accident.
Further it contended that, falsely and without conducting proper investigation, the driver of the offending car has been Charge sheeted by the jurisdictional police by colluding with the Petitioner.

Further it contended that the driver of the offending car was not holding valid and effective driving license at the time of accident and the car was not having valid Registration Certificate, Permit and Fitness Certificate as on the date of accident.
Thereby the insured has breached the contract of Insurance.
Hence, it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
On these grounds, the Respondent No.3 has prayed to dismiss the Petition against it.
4. On the rival Pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following Issues:

ISSUES 1. Whether the Petitioner proves that his Maruthi Suzuki Swift Car bearing Reg.No.KA 51MJ7383 got damaged in a Road Traffic SCCH 15 6 MVC No.1082/2023 Accident that occurred on 09.01.2022 at about 7.30 p.m., on Bengaluru - Kanakapura main road, at Lakshmipura, in front of Navagrama,
Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the Innova Car bearing Reg.No.KA 01AE0728 by its driver?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for?
If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay ?
3. What Order or Award?
5. In order to substantiate the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 10 documents at Ex.P.1 to P.10 and closed his side evidence.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.3 did not choose to lead evidence.

6. During the course of Arguments, the Learned Counsel for the Respondent No.3 has relied on the following decisions:
SCCH 15 7 MVC No.1082/2023 1. ILR 2000 KAR 2009, in between Karnaaka State Road Transport Corporation Vs. George Ninum 2. 2005 ACJ 1332, between Harkhu Bai and others Vs. Jiyaram and others.

sentences.text: I have heard the arguments of the learned Counsel for the Petitioner and the learned Counsel for the Respondents and perused the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record.

8. My answer to the above Issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No. 2 : In the Negative  Issue No. 3 : As per the Final Order  for the following :
 SCCH 15 8 MVC No.1082/2023  REASONS 9.
Issue No.1:

It is the case of the Petitioner that his Maruthi Suzuki Swift Car bearing Reg.No.KA 51MJ7383 got damaged in the Motor Vehicle Accident that occurred on 09.01.2022 at about 7.30 p.m., by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Innova Car bearing Reg.No.KA01AE 0728.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.3 has denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car.
10. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 10 documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P10.
P.W.1 has reiterated the Petition averments in his chiefaffidavit.
Ex.P1 is the Copy of FIR, Ex.P2 is the Complaint, Ex.P.3 is the copy of Order sheet in CC No.7996/2022.
Ex.P4 is the Service Estimation.
Ex.P5 is the Charge sheet.
Ex.P6 to 10 are the Certified copy of Order sheet SCCH 15 9 MVC No.1082/2023 in CC No.7996/2022, Police Notice with Reply, Indemnity bonds and Statement.

11. Upon going through the Ex.P1 & 2 i.e., FIR and Complaint, which shows that on the Complaint lodged by one Mukesh M.E S/o Ishwar Gowda, before Kaggalipura Police Station, the PSI of the concerned Police Station has registered the case against the driver of Innova Car bearing Reg.No.KA01 AE0728 for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 of IPC.
Ex.P.3 is the copy of Order sheet in CC No.7996/2022 on the file of IInd ACJM, Bengaluru Rural District.
Ex.P4 is the Service Estimation.

Ex.P5 is the Certified copy of the Charge Sheet which shows that after thorough investigation, the PSI of Kaggalipura Police Station has submitted Chargesheet against the driver of the offending car for the offences punishable under Sec. 279, 337 and 338 of IPC.
Ex.P6 to 10 are the Certified copy of Order sheet in CC No.7996/2022, Police Notice with Reply, Indemnity bonds and Statement.

sentences.text: 4 12. PW.1 is subjected for cross examination by the Learned Counsel for the Respondent No.3.

But,
nothing could elicited to disbelieve the testimony of the PW.1.
In respect of the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Innova Car.

13. Though the Respondent No.3 has taken contention that the accident does not occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car, it did not examine any witness to substantiate its contentions.
Moreover, after thorough investigation, the I.O. has filed Chargesheet against the driver of the offending car.

Further, Ex.P3 & 6 are the Certified copy of Order sheet in CC No.7996/2022 on the file of IInd ACJM, Bengaluru Rural District, which shows that the driver of the offending car had pleaded guilty and paid fine.

Therefore, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the Petitioner has proved that the accident has caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car and due to which Swift car was damaged.

Accordingly, I answer Issue SCCH 15 11 MVC No.1082/2023 No.1 in the 'Affirmative'.
14. Issue No.2:

As per detailed discussion made in Issue No.1, this Tribunal comes to the conclusion that the alleged accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Innova Car.
It is the contention of the Petitioner that in the said accident, his car was damaged.

He deposed in his evidence that he is the RC owner of the car bearing Reg.No.KA51MJ7383.
15.
During the crossexamination of PW.1, he deposed that he can produce RC of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA51MJ 7383 and he can produce IMV report.
But, it is worth to note here that PW.1 has not produced RC to show that he is the RC owner of the car bearing Reg.No.KA51MJ7383 at the time of the accident.

Further, PW.1 has also deposed in the cross examination that he can produce copy of Insurance policy of his car and he can also produce the Survey report and also he can produce the Receipt for the payment of repair charges.

During the course of argument, the Learned Counsel for the Respondent No.3 has relied on the following decisions:
1) ILR 2000 KAR 2009 in between Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation Vs George Ninum,
wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has pleased to held as under:
"Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (Central Act No.59 of 1988) - Section 168 - Claim petition of a person claiming to be the owner of the car, for compensation for repair of the car was allowed rejecting the contention of the KSRTC that claimant's ownership of the car and Special Damages are not proved -

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Held - in the absence of any material to show that the claimant was the owner of the car, the claim petition itself was not maintainable - Mere producing of documents is not sufficient to prove Special Damages.
Such documents has to be proved.
Mere production of document is not a proof of its contents."

Seenappa Reddy G.N vs William on 10 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106251547/
5 2) 2005 ACJ 1332 in between Harkhu Bai and others Vs. Jiyaram and others, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has pleased to held as under:
"Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, Sec.166 - Claim application - Damage to property - Estoppel - Truck 'B' was damaged in accident due to negligence of driver of truck 'A' -
owner of truck 'B' received compensation in full and final settlement of his claim from his insurance company - whether the owner fo truck 'B' can claim compensation from insurance company of SCCH 15 13 MVC No.1082/2023 truck 'A' - Held: no.
3) 2006 ACJ 2566 in between D.I. Narayana Swamy and another Vs. National Insurance Co. Ltd., and another, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has pleased to held as under:
"Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, Sections 165 and 166 - Claims Tribunal - Jurisdiction - claim application - maintainability of Subrogation - Damage to maxicab in collusion with offending truck - Insurance Company of maxicab has reimbursed the damages to the insured Whether insurance company of maxicab under its right of subrogation can maintain a claim against owner and insurance company of truck before claim tribunal - Held: no; claim to enforce subrogation rights is outside the jurisdiction of the claims tribunal.

sentences.text: 17. I have gone through the above decisions.
In ILR 2000 KAR 2009, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has pleased to observed that, "Mere production of a document is no proof of the claim at all.
The author of those two documents is not examined.
The mechanic who repaired the car is not examined.
Absolutely, there is no actual expenditure incurred by the alleged owner.
It is not sufficient to award compensation SCCH 15 14 MVC No.1082/2023 specially in the case of special damages, in the absence of these essential materials before the Tribunal.
Accordingly, the appeal is allowed and award passed by the Tribunal is set aside."

18. In the decision reported in 2005 ACJ 1332, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has pleased to observed that "The vehicle being insured with one of the other insurance companies, the damage was assessed and paid.
The order passed by the Tribunal further shows that the payment was received by the claimant in full and final settlement of his claim without any reservation or demur.

In the absence of any material to show that the claim paid by the other insurance company represented a part only of the total damage, the Tribunal was justified in rejecting the claim for any further payment."
19.

In the decision reported in 2006 ACJ 2556, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has pleased to observed that, "The Petitioner No.1 has already been reimbursed by his SCCH 15 15 MVC No.1082/2023 insurer.

Hence, the Tribunal rightly comes to the conclusion that the claim against the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle on the same cause amounts to duplicated claim and accordingly, dismissed the petition."

sentences.text: In the instant case the Petitioner neither in the Petition nor in his evidence has stated whether he has received claim from his insurance company or not.
It is important to note here that the Petitioner has not produced R.C to show that he is the owner of the car bearing Reg.No.KA51MJ 7383 at the time of the accident.
Hence, the Petitioner failed to prove his ownership as on the date of accident.
Further, he has not produced IMV report which is the material document to show that which parts of the alleged car has been damaged.
Further, the Petitioner has produced only Service estimate and he has not produced any Receipt to show the payment towards the repairs of alleged car.
Further the Petitioner has not produced Survey report and he has also not examined the concerned SCCH 15 16 MVC No.1082/2023 owner of the garage, where he alleged to be repaired the vehicle.
Hence, in the absence of these documents, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the Petitioner is not entitled any compensation.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 is in the "Negative".
21. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby dismissed with costs.
Draw Award accordingly.
